name: GrapheneDB
tagline: Managed hosting for Neo4j Community Edition on dedicated cloud instances, with backups and replicas.
description: GrapheneDB is a hosted service that runs Neo4j Community Edition databases on dedicated instances in a private cloud, operated by GrapheneDB Labs since about 2013. It adds the operational pieces Community Edition lacks out of the box: scheduled and hot snapshots, clone and restore, read replicas, query logs and metrics, VPC peering, IP allow-lists, encryption at rest and in transit, a management API and, recently, an MCP server for AI assistants. Pricing is pay-as-you-go from about $44 a month or by subscription, with $50 of trial credit. It suits teams that want Cypher and the Neo4j ecosystem without Enterprise licensing or managing servers; for clustering and Enterprise features look at Neo4j Aura instead.

license.name: Proprietary service (hosts GPLv3 Neo4j Community Edition)

pricing.notes: $50 trial credit; Gold support plan $50/month; no Neo4j license or data-transfer fees.

scale.notes: Single primary per database, sized up to 512 GB RAM and 48 vCPU, plus optional read replicas.

strengths: Neo4j Community without running servers, with backups and snapshots handled
Read replicas and VPC peering on top of Community Edition
No Neo4j license fees and no data-transfer charges
Transparent per-instance pricing with a cost estimator
weaknesses: Community Edition limits: no causal clustering or Enterprise security features
Write capacity bounded by a single primary instance
Smaller vendor than Neo4j itself; region list is not public
useCases: Production Neo4j apps on a budget
Recommendation and social graphs for startups
Managed graph backends for knowledge-graph prototypes
notIdealFor: Very large graphs that exceed one instance
